tasks.short: Maintain radio contact with aircraft commanders

steps.what: Monitor the actual air-to-ground and point-to-point radio traffic, identify the aircraft commander and relevant operational context, and clarify any unclear received message.

Determine and immediately check the exact next radio message, aircraft identity, channel, current facts and the specialist's authority before transmission using the operational radio equipment {OTHER}.
Maintain air-to-ground and point-to-point radio contact with aircraft commanders by transmitting the exact checked immediate message through the operational radio equipment {OTHER}.
Listen for and verify the actual acknowledgement or readback, resolve discrepancies and continue the exchange using the operational radio equipment {OTHER}.

Write any operationally required significant-exchange entry in the airfield operations log {OPS_SYSTEM}, checking actual time, aircraft identity, message substance and acknowledgement against the real exchange.
Save the exact checked significant-exchange entry in {OPS_SYSTEM}.

tasks.design: Retain human radio communication and the actual significant-exchange log. Test existing radio and {OPS_SYSTEM} recording facilities first; automatic voice recording is already system runtime and does not remove the specialist's listening or judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Messages depend on immediate context and verified acknowledgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing radios and log tools already support this exchange.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising ambiguity and changing conditions without exceeding the specialist's authority.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist listens, checks the exact message and resolves readback discrepancies.

ambition.what: No automatic radio operator is proposed.

tasks.altitude: Radio responsibility and the specialist's week remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Immediate operational radio communication and acknowledgement remain human work; existing recording runtime does not establish a labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary: the specialist's radio contact and its required significant-event log, not aircraft control or another controller's clearance work. Radio equipment is the {OTHER} system in s1-s4.

Commanders and actual operations supply aircraft identity, current message, time, context and acknowledgement. The specialist checks them live and manually resolves ambiguity; no prepared transcript or inferred acknowledgement is free.

s1-s4 repeat for each next message. s2 is the ordinary immediate check of an already-formulated exact message, not a software approval queue. Any message or context change invalidates the transmission gate.
The separate completed-log check in s5 gates s6 without additional self-approval labour; changes invalidate it. No routine word-for-word manual transcript is invented.
Shares are illustrative E1 estimates, not measured baseline times. Record work is separated and fully retained before concluding zero; zero upkeep follows from introducing no change.
unknowns: Which significant exchanges require a manual log
research_questions: Is there real duplicate log entry beyond the existing recording facilities?

already_counted.description: Listening, exact-message checks, transmission, acknowledgement and actual log writing/save remain fully counted.

approvals.approved_version: Exact immediate message, aircraft, channel and context checked in s2
Exact exchange log contents and record checked in s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Live communication and the separate actual log remain; no repeated removable operation is established.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Procure the required current flight planning publications, operations publications, charts, maps and weather information from authorised aviation information services {OTHER}; native subscriptions and linked views reduce repeated retrieval while retaining missing-feed follow-up.
inputs: actual information request and operation scope

steps.what: Verify source authority, publication cycle, effective periods, weather issue time, geographic coverage and applicability to the actual operation, resolving gaps or conflicts with the responsible source.
inputs: actual information request and operation scope

steps.what: Produce the requested operation-information pack in {DOCS}, using native templates and source links to assemble the verified publications, charts and weather references without rewriting or omitting original notices.
inputs: actual information request and operation scope

steps.what: Check the complete pack against original sources and the requested operation, including effective times, map versions, completeness, access expiry and exact intended recipients.
Save the exact checked operation-information pack in {DOCS}.
Provide the exact checked information pack to the identified aircraft-operation recipients through the authorised aviation information system {OTHER}.
Explain the actual pack and its limits to the recipients, clarify operational questions and resolve a new or stale information issue with its authorised source rather than inventing an answer.
outputs: actual information briefing and clarified limits

tasks.design: Configure authorised source subscriptions and native {DOCS} pack templates before custom integration. Retain original information and specialist applicability checks, followed by separate final save, provision and actual briefing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information sources have different versions, effective periods and coverage.
tasks.enabler_now: Native subscriptions and controlled links can reduce retrieval and pack assembly without generating aviation facts.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing whether the actual operation has complete current information.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist resolves applicability and communicates limitations.

ambition.what: No autonomous flight planning or clearance service is proposed.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated retrieval leaves attention for stale or conflicting sources; flight-operation authority does not expand.

reach.learn: Understand operational information applicability without taking over pilot decisions.

evidence.claim: Native source subscriptions and document templates can support controlled aviation-information retrieval and assembly.

assumptions: Boundary: obtaining, producing and providing current information, not buying a new licence, issuing official aviation publications or deciding a flight plan. Existing authorised source access is required and its actual maintenance is counted.

Source services produce publication ID/revision, authority, effective dates, geographic scope and weather issue/validity times. Requesters supply actual operation scope and recipients. s1-s2 retain manual retrieval and clarification for missing or failed feeds; no source extraction is assumed free.
No model ranks away or hides notices. Native tools are tested first; system download/runtime already automated earns no human saving.
The completed-pack check in s4 binds each requested save/provision gate. Updated information, operation scope or recipients invalidate both without an added approval stage.
Shares and reductions are illustrative E1 estimates, not measured baselines; actual aviation approval and access requirements must be verified locally.
unknowns: Authorised feed availability and current native subscriptions
Actual information distribution and validation requirements
research_questions: How much active retrieval and pack copying remains after current subscriptions?

already_counted.description: Source exceptions, applicability review, pack checks, final actions and actual briefing remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain authorised source links and effective-period/template checks.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final information pack and source versions checked in s4
Exact pack, validity window and recipient set checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 27.5 less 2 upkeep yields net 25.5 when retrieval and pack assembly repeat manually. Already-integrated source access yields little or no new gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Anticipate equipment for evacuation and cargo flights

steps.what: Clarify the actual air evacuation or cargo mission with the responsible flight, medical or cargo personnel, including mission timing, aircraft constraints, patient or load needs and uncertainty.

Find current compatible equipment specifications and actual availability in {OPS_SYSTEM} and controlled aircraft documents {DOCS}; native equipment and aircraft views reduce repeated navigation while retaining confirmation with the actual equipment owner.
inputs: actual controlled equipment and aircraft records

steps.what: Anticipate aircraft equipment needs for air evacuation and cargo flights, assessing compatibility, mission contingencies and gaps with responsible specialists without making clinical, airworthiness or aircraft load-approval decisions outside the role.
outputs: reasoned equipment needs and unresolved gaps

steps.what: Write the actual equipment-needs list in {DOCS}, including mission reference, quantities, compatibility limits, timing and unresolved gaps, and check the completed list and intended receiving coordinator.
inputs: reasoned equipment needs and unresolved gaps

steps.what: Save the exact checked mission equipment-needs list in {DOCS}.
Send the exact checked equipment-needs list to the identified mission coordinator through {EMAIL}, with unresolved gaps explicitly retained.

tasks.design: Configure native equipment and aircraft-record views in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {DOCS}. Retain actual mission clarification, specialist judgement and the needs list, with a separate final save and handoff rather than an automatic equipment order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mission needs and equipment compatibility require context beyond stock availability.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views can make controlled compatibility and availability records easier to locate.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual evacuation or cargo requirements and uncertain mission conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist anticipates gaps and involves the responsible clinical and flight experts.

ambition.what: No new mission type or autonomous equipment allocation is assumed.

tasks.altitude: Shorter lookup leaves more attention for mission contingencies; operational authority remains unchanged.

reach.learn: Distinguish equipment availability from aircraft compatibility and approved loading.

evidence.claim: Native equipment-record views support lookup without deciding mission suitability.

assumptions: Boundary: anticipating and communicating needs, not procuring, reserving, installing or loading equipment. Other roles' clinical, aircraft and equipment work earns no saving.

Mission owners supply mission ID, timing, aircraft constraints and actual patient/cargo requirements. Equipment owners supply item IDs, quantities, availability and controlled compatibility references. s1-s3 retain direct clarification and manual reconciliation of missing fields; no clean mission feed is assumed.

The actual list is authored in s4. Its ordinary completed-list check binds each requested save/send gate without additional approval time; any mission, equipment, timing or recipient change invalidates both.
Shares and reductions are illustrative E1 estimates. Native views are tested first; existing stock-system runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Current compatibility records and availability accuracy
research_questions: Does repeated equipment lookup consume active time beyond mission judgement?

already_counted.description: Mission elicitation, source checks, suitability reasoning, actual list writing and final actions remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain equipment links and controlled-reference versions.

approvals.approved_version: Exact mission equipment list and record checked in s4
Exact needs, unresolved gaps and mission recipient checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 6 less 1 upkeep yields net 5 when repeated lookup exists. Already-linked equipment views yield no additional gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Post airfield visual and status boards

steps.what: Obtain the actual current airfield status from responsible operations sources, checking issue time, affected location, source identity and any missing or conflicting update.
Determine which status applies to each board field and validity period, resolve inconsistent reports and decide what can be displayed within the specialist's actual authority.
inputs: actual board scope and posting rules

steps.what: Prepare the status cards or board text from the determined contents; for a currently manual board, native digital-board templates in {OPS_SYSTEM} would reduce repeated formatting and copying while retaining entry and correction of actual source facts.
Check the complete proposed board against the actual sources, including each location, status meaning, issue and expiry times, destination board and information that must remain visible.
inputs: actual board scope and posting rules

steps.what: Post visual display boards and status boards by placing the exact checked contents on the actual board; a configured digital board in {OPS_SYSTEM} would publish only that approved snapshot instead of the specialist physically replacing cards.

tasks.design: Test a native digital status-board facility in {OPS_SYSTEM} before building a display app. Keep actual status collection and judgement human, prepare a complete preview, and publish only the exact specialist-checked snapshot with visible validity and a manual fallback.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual cards require repeated copying and physical posting after status is already determined.
tasks.enabler_now: Native display templates can render and publish an explicitly approved board version.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting source status, stale information and display outages.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist establishes what the board can legitimately state.

ambition.what: No automatic operational decision or broader status authority is claimed.

tasks.altitude: Less manual card handling leaves more attention for status conflicts; source verification remains human.

reach.learn: Validate status provenance, display scope and safe manual fallback.

evidence.claim: Digital board templates can render and post an exact approved snapshot instead of manual card replacement.

assumptions: Boundary: posting a currently manual airfield board, from actual status collection to displayed contents. This is an E1 scenario, not a claim that this organisation has paper boards; already-digital posting has no new labour return.

Responsible operations sources supply location or asset ID, status, issue time, effective/expiry period and source identity. The specialist obtains and verifies those facts in s1-s2 and manually enters missing fields in s3; no clean live feed is assumed.

s3 produces the complete proposed contents before s4 checks them. In the digital design s4 checks the rendered final snapshot and destination, and the requested posting gate binds that exact snapshot; any changed fact or validity period invalidates it.

Only current active copying and physical posting lose time. Native system runtime and existing automatic display refresh earn no saving; outages and unverified status use the retained manual collection and posting fallback, included in upkeep.
Actual display access, operational acceptance and national rules must be verified before use. No model generates status or hides a stale source.
unknowns: Whether current boards are physical or already digital
Native display capability and operational fallback requirements
research_questions: Does measured card preparation and replacement justify digital-board setup after validation and outage costs?

already_counted.description: Actual source collection, status judgement, data entry corrections and final board review remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain display templates and access, check stale indicators and handle occasional manual outage posting.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final rendered status snapshot, validity period and destination board checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 27 less 2 upkeep yields net 25 for actual manual card formatting and posting. An already-digital board yields zero new saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Information retrieval and manual board posting may shrink; radio contact and operational judgement remain accountable.
reach: Learn source-validity checks and controlled display publishing.
role.ambitious_version: Use less repeated posting work to identify stale or conflicting operational information sooner.
